name: Pilatus P-3
summary: Swiss tandem two-seat primary trainer of the 1950s with a flat-six piston engine and retractable gear, the forerunner of the PC-7, flown by the Swiss Air Force and now by private owners.

wings: Low, straight, tapered wing with squared tips
Clean laminar-flow shape with no tip tanks
engines: Single six-cylinder flat engine in a smooth cowl
fuselage: Tandem seats under a long sliding canopy
Slim fuselage with a pronounced dorsal line behind the canopy
tail: Horizontal tail mounted on the fuselage

tellTales: Slim tandem two-seater with a long sliding canopy and retractable nose-wheel gear
Smooth flat-six cowl and a straight tapered low wing with no tip tanks
Looks like a piston-powered forerunner of the Pilatus turboprops

confusedWith.howToTell: The SF.260 has permanent wingtip tanks and a thinner fuselage; the P-3 has plain wingtips.
The T-34 has a different canopy, a higher stance and a heavier, more rounded fuselage; the P-3 is slimmer.
The PC-7 has a turboprop nose with a chin scoop and a taller canopy; the P-3 has a smooth piston cowl.
